finding: The worst quarter of batches by COPQ share of revenue carries most of the quality bill.
evidence: 256 of 1,000 batches hold 49.9% of total COPQ (1,733,355 of 3,472,487).
action: Review the high cost batch list with plant quality leads this week.

finding: Batches below the Cpk target cost more to correct.
evidence: COPQ is 2.96% of revenue for 119 batches below Cpk 1.33 against 2.32% for 881 batches at or above it.
action: Prioritise capability work on the lines producing the low Cpk batches.

finding: Plants differ clearly in cost of poor quality.
evidence: Plant B (Texas) runs at 2.51% of revenue (358 batches) against 2.28% at Plant C (Monterrey) (350 batches).
action: Share the practices of the best plant with the worst plant this month.

finding: One product family is the costliest to get right.
evidence: Injection Molded Housings carries COPQ of 3.46% of revenue (190 batches) against 1.81% for Precision Shafts.
action: Review the process plan and inspection points for the costliest family.

finding: Material suppliers show a gap in downstream cost.
evidence: Batches on S2 show COPQ of 3.18% of revenue (305 batches) against 2.06% on S1.
action: Raise the gap in the next supplier review and request corrective actions.

finding: Special cause events are followed by higher quality cost.
evidence: 47 special cause batches carry COPQ of 4.20% of revenue against 2.30% for 953 others.
action: Hold a short cause review for every special cause event.

finding: Failures reaching the customer are a measurable part of the quality bill.
evidence: External failure cost is 70.4% of total COPQ (2,445,416 of 3,472,487).
action: Check final inspection coverage for the product families with most external failure cost.

finding: A small set of batches is statistically unusual.
evidence: 50 batches (5.0% of the dataset) are flagged; 98.0% of them are high cost batches against 21.8% elsewhere.
action: Walk through the flagged batches with the shift supervisors.

evidence: 10 batches are P1 urgent and 990 are P2 high out of 1,000.
action: Assign an owner to every P1 batch today.

finding: Process inputs known during production give an early warning of costly batches.
evidence: Held-out test AUC 0.91 (naive baseline 0.50) with Product_Family as the leading input.
action: Use the score to select batches for extra inspection before shipping.

finding: The high risk segment holds a disproportionate share of cost.
evidence: 29 high risk batches (2.9%) hold 6.2% of COPQ.
action: Start improvement projects on the process patterns in this segment.
